Subject: Order Form v3 — venue & injunctive relief

Grace — attaching our redlines to the Order Form and a short note on governing law/venue. Two asks from Legal: 1) Governing law be New York, with courts of New York for any court proceedings; 2) carve out for equitable relief to allow emergency injunctive relief in courts (we’d prefer no mandatory arbitration for injunctive/urgent preservation).

We understand Redwood’s preference for arbitration for most disputes — our counsel is worried about delays for urgent IP/data preservation. If Redwood will agree to an injunctive carveout (preserving right to seek immediate relief in NY courts) we can accept arbitration for other disputes and move forward with a small one-time integration PO.

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order Form v3 — venue & injunctive relief

Tim — thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. Quick response while I pull legal in: we (Redwood) typically require arbitration for dispute resolution to reduce litigation exposure and to keep process predictable for both parties. That said, we already have a limited carveout in some enterprise orders to permit provisional equitable relief (injunctions) in court when necessary for preservation of IP or customer data.

I'm looping in Kimberly (GC) and Marissa (Account Exec) to propose a practical fallback that protects both sides and avoids reopening the MSA wholesale. Proposed path: 
- Arbitration as primary dispute-resolution forum (per MSA).
- Explicit carveout: either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in NY state or federal courts to preserve rights or prevent immediate harm; such action does not waive arbitration for the merits.
- Narrow definition of "immediate harm": unauthorized data exfiltration, misappropriation of proprietary model weights, or actions likely to make arbitration remedies moot.

If that sounds workable we can produce a redline to the Order Form and MSA paragraph that implements it (one short clause).

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
(attachment: placeholder OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-12-02T11:10:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Order Form v3 — venue & injunctive relief

Folks — thanks for the context, Tim. A few legal points and a suggested redline below. We want to limit precedent exposure while giving Orion the operational certainty you need for urgent preservation. Key considerations: 1) carveouts should be explicit and narrow; 2) pick a jurisdiction that Redwood already accepts in enterprise orders (NY is acceptable for US enterprise customers); 3) preserve Redwood's ability to compel arbitration for the merits and to seek interim measures in the forum specified.

Suggested clause (one paragraph to add to the Order Form / MSA where dispute resolution is discussed):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in the courts of the State of New York or the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York to preserve rights or prevent irreparable harm, including but not limited to protection of confidential information, proprietary model weights, or customer data. The availability of such provisional relief shall not constitute a waiver of any party's obligation to pursue arbitration for the final resolution of disputes under this Agreement."

Operational notes for Sales: if Orion asks for alternative forum language (their comment favors NY courts), we should accept NY as drafted. If they request forum outside NY (e.g., state of their incorporation), escalate to Legal. Also confirm SOC2 and encryption at rest details (Tim provided SOC2_summary.pdf).

I'll draft a tracked redline to both the Order Form and the MSA paragraph and send back. Marissa, please verify the timeline — they want to close the PO this month.

Kimberly Park
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MSA_GovLaw_Summary.docx)
